requirements.description: Research must focus on next-generation AI agents defined as autonomous systems powered by large AI language models (LLMs) or large multimodal models, capable of planning, tool use, and autonomous action to achieve specified goals from high-level instructions.
AI agent design must incorporate structured planning and reasoning methods to manage complex multi-step tasks, and be equipped with appropriate validation and monitoring techniques.

AI agent design must incorporate effective memory and state management, achieved through a balanced integration of short-term and external long-term memory solutions, to maintain coherent long-term interactions.
AI agent design must integrate external tools and APIs to overcome limitations in large AI models and enhance agent performance in tasks requiring accuracy and reliability.
All proposals must incorporate mechanisms for assessing and demonstrating progress, including qualitative and quantitative KPIs, benchmarking, and progress monitoring.
Communicable results must be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
Projects must link to the resources offered by the AI Factories, including the Data Labs.
All proposals must allocate tasks for cohesion activities with the ADRA partnership and the CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18 (GenAI4EU central Hub).
Proposals should build on or seek collaboration with relevant projects and develop synergies with other relevant International, European, national, or regional initiatives.
When possible, proposals should build on and reuse public results from relevant previous funded actions.
Results may be validated in the Testing and Experiment Facilities (TEFs) and further deployed via the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).

Research may focus on enhancing AI agent autonomy through advanced self-planning and self-optimization capabilities, enabling agents to improve their decision-making and strategic planning (optional research direction).
Research may focus on innovation in memory-augmented AI agents to facilitate robust long-term reasoning and lifelong learning (optional research direction).

Research may focus on developing advanced multi-agent frameworks specifically tailored for collaborative agents, including research on AI agent frameworks based on mixed AI architectures (optional research direction).
Research may focus on advancing multimodal reasoning capabilities to enable real-world applications (optional research direction).

Proposals should demonstrate applicability to at least one Apply AI sector. Portfolio-level coverage across three sectors (healthcare, advanced manufacturing, in-vehicle autonomous driving) is enforced through a procedure exception at the call level, not as a per-proposal requirement.
requirements.inference_note: The procedure_exceptions field states grants will be awarded to ensure at least one project in each of the three sectors. This implies each proposal should identify and demonstrate its target sector focus, though all three sectors need not be addressed by a single proposal. The mandatory field is false because the sector targeting operates as a portfolio selection mechanism rather than a per-proposal scope mandate.
